method: Derived from direct SERP observation. observedVolume is null for every query BY POLICY — no keyword tool exists and nothing is estimated.
governingFinding: The residential/commercial boundary that matters is NOT the words 'rental' versus 'apartment building' — Google treats those as interchangeable in this market. The real boundary is the BUYER POOL and the VALUATION METHOD, and it is legally and financially real: above four units the asset leaves residential comp-based appraisal and residential financing (FHFA 12 CFR 1282.1) and moves to income-based valuation. The SERP partially respects this already.
riskDirection: ONE-WAY. Existing residential pages are NOT at risk from the SERP — they are at risk from our own copy choices. A commercial multifamily page written in landlord-exit language ('tired of managing tenants', 'no repairs, no fees') will be classified as another residential page and will compete with our own. The reverse is very unlikely: commercial marketplaces hold the large-multifamily slots and a residential page has nothing to rank on there.

enforcementRules: PUT THE UNIT LINE ON THE PAGE, VISIBLY. A commercial multifamily page must state that it is about five units and up, priced on rent roll and NOI. A page that merely says 'we buy multifamily' is a residential lookalike and will be classified as one.

VOCABULARY IS THE CLASSIFIER. Rent roll, NOI, cap rate, estoppel, T-12 and WALT belong on the commercial page. Landlord-exit language — 'tired of managing tenants', 'no repairs, no fees', 'sell your rental fast' — must NOT appear there.

Never write 'five units is legally commercial'. The FHFA boundary governs housing finance; Census treats two units as multifamily and HUD varies between 2, 5 and 8. State which system a boundary belongs to.
Duplex, triplex and fourplex stay residential in both copy and internal linking.
